rules.statement: A feature turned on by a property or by the host's classpath never runs without what it needs (its module, its REQUIRED listener, its Redis connection): startup fails and names what to add. A module no feature uses needs nothing: a service behind a gateway (`cosec.pipeline.mode=gateway`) with JWT off, which wires no Redis data plane, starts without Redis although `cosec-cocache` is on its classpath.

rules.statement: On a Spring Cloud Gateway host in enforce mode, startup fails when an actuator endpoint other than health, of any kind (an operation endpoint, or a controller endpoint such as Spring Cloud Gateway's own gateway), is exposed over HTTP on the application port (management.server.port unset or the application's), naming the endpoints, what to set and the documentation, unless cosec.gateway.unprotected-endpoints lists it; that property never accepts gateway, wherever it is served. On a separate management port, or with the management server off, any endpoint may be exposed.

rules.statement: The starter's startup checks run whatever spring.main.lazy-initialization says: every module check (STA-1), the actuator endpoint check (STA-2), the eviction policy check and monitor (SNP-3), the replica read check (RC1-47), the API key membership check (IDN-6), the pipeline mode check, the unknown property check and the control plane's own-authorization check fail startup under lazy initialization as they do without it, and the components that keep watching once the host runs (the eviction policy monitor, shadow reporting, control-plane maintenance, the listeners' metrics) start at startup. Each of them is a StartupTask bean, which lazy initialization never defers; no auto-configuration of the starter declares one any other way. A configuration none of them refuses starts under lazy initialization.

rules.statement: On every port a host opens, nothing the application serves answers without passing CoSec. A WebFlux application's management server (management.server.port different from the application's) is under the pipeline, as its application port is: its probes, and what it inherits of the application's, functional routes and the control API among them. A WebMvc application's management server serves only actuator's endpoints: a controller, a functional route and the control API are not served there. A gateway's management server serves actuator's endpoints and, when the control plane is on, the control API under its own pipeline; the gateway's routes are served there only where Spring Cloud Gateway cannot tell the port apart (a random management port), and then under the gateway's filter. With one port, the probes are requests like any other.

rules.statement: When the application declares a CorsConfigurationSource (the bean of its own stack's interface; Spring MVC's own HandlerMappingIntrospector is not a declaration) and registers no CorsFilter or CorsWebFilter of its own, the starter registers a CORS filter immediately before the pipeline's on Spring MVC and WebFlux. A preflight (OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method) is then answered by that filter and is not decided: no policy, rate limit, blacklist, audit, decision event or metric sees it. An OPTIONS that is no preflight is decided as before; a request that is not a preflight is decided as before, and a refusal carries the CORS headers; an origin the source does not allow is refused by the filter before the pipeline. Without the bean nothing is registered and a preflight is decided as http:OPTIONS for an anonymous caller.
